newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin eyes non-combative power-sharing in 1988.
newsitem.headline: Jospin eyes non-combative power-sharing in 1988.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, eyeing possible victory in 1998 elections, said on Wednesday that power-sharing with President Jacques Chirac would not be combative but based on "a voters' pact".
"Winning the general elections is possible. It won't be easy," Jospin, head of the country's biggest opposition force, told the newspaper Le Figaro in an interview.
"It won't be a combative cohabitation, but a cohabitation based on a pact. If we win in 1998, we will apply the pact that we will have agreed with the people in the election campaign," Jospin said.
He added that the Socialists would respect institutional and constitutional prerogatives, including those of the President who has special influence over foreign and defence policy.

But Jospin criticised Chirac for pushing France back towards NATO. "It would be better to work on the issue of European defence rather than go back under the American umbrella, at a time when it has new hegemonic temptations."

"...It is quite possible that if and when we take power, the President can only note the failure of his policy. If that is the case, there will be no major problem," Jospin said. He refused to say whether the Socialists would bow to the President if the matter was still controversial.

Jospin has criticised Chirac for agreeing to a fuller role in NATO without winning any concessions from the United States, 30 years after General Charles de Gaulle pulled France out of its military wing.

A Franco-German defence document signed by Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in December said their first commitment was to defend NATO and urged a dialogue on the role of nuclear deterrence in European defence.
